title: The Intel 4004: Fetch-Decode-Execute on a Single Chip (1971)
explainer: The fetch-decode-execute cycle this lesson describes was first packed into a single commercial chip by the Intel 4004 in 1971, a 4-bit CPU with roughly 2,300 transistors designed by Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, and Stanley Mazor at Intel together with Masatoshi Shima of Busicom, originally for a desktop calculator. Before the 4004, equivalent sequencing logic needed multiple separate chips or room-sized machines; fitting the whole clocked fetch-decode-execute sequence onto one piece of silicon is what created 'the microprocessor' as a product category.
